newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China plane lands near Manila, no word on defector.
newsitem.headline: China plane lands near Manila, no word on defector.

text.p: An unscheduled Boeing 737 plane arrived at Clark airbase in the Philippines from Xiamen, China, on Tuesday but it was not immediately known if North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop was aboard, a Manila airport official said.

Alger Ramo, supervising air traffic controller at Manila's international airport, said "several people" got off the plane after it touched down at 12:23 p.m. (0423 GMT), basing his comments on information he received from Clark controllers.
He said the plane sought airport clearance only a few minutes before it landed at Clark, just north of the capital.
Desiree Domingo, air traffic controller at nearby Subic Bay airport, also confirmed the arrival of the flight from China.
Hwang, North Korea's top ideologue and most senior official to defect from the Stalinist homeland, sought shelter at the South Korean consulate in Beijing on February 12.
Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said last week his country was prepared to accept Hwang in transit if he was allowed to leave Beijing for South Korea.

"We saw a lot of people coming down from the aircraft. We are now asking the pilot for details," Ramo quoted a Clark air controller as saying after the mysterious plane landed at the former U.S. air base 80 km (50 miles) north of Manila.
There was no immediate information on the identities of the plane's occupants.

A China Southern Airlines flight CZ379 carrying a mysterious VIP passenger took off on Tuesday morning from the southeastern city of Xiamen, bound for the Philippines. It was not immediately clear if it was the same plane that landed at Clark.

The passenger had earlier taken a special dawn flight from a Beijing military airport, his route matching the one Hwang was expected to take when he ended weeks of diplomatic limbo at the centre of a crisis between China and the two rival Koreas.
"I can't say if (Hwang) is on board," said one airline official in Xiamen shortly after China Southern Flight CZ379 took off from the port city for the two-hour flight to Manila.

Earlier on Tuesday, a Philippine foreign ministry spokesman said Foreign Underscretary Rodolfo Severino would make a statement on the matter but later said Severino had been called away to a cabinet meeting by President Fidel Ramos and would not be able to meet reporters as planned.
"No statement today. I hope by tomorrow," Oscar Valenzuela said.
Asked to confirm if Hwang was on the plane, he said "I don't know".
On Monday, a senior South Korean official said Hwang would stay in a third country "for a considerable period of time" before coming to South Korea.

Hwang's Beijing defection had muddied ties between China and the two Koreas, bitter rivals since the 1950-1953 Korean War, and forced Beijing to choose between a new capitalist friend in the South and an old communist ally in the North.
